Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
1036 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

.SYNOPSIS...20/1019 PM.

Dry and cooler weather is expected through Sunday morning. AThere
will be a chance of light rain Sunday and Sunday night. Light 
rain is possible again Tuesday night into Wednesday. Thanksgiving 
will be dry and warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (FRI-MON)...20/849 PM.

***UPDATE***

An upper disturbance is moving Central California to southern 
interior California tonight. As this occurs, a short wave ridge 
will pop up behind it over SW California, before another 
disturbance approaches for Saturday night through Sunday. 

Expect another chilly night across the area tonight, with areas 
of frost over the far interior valleys, including the Antelope and
Cuyama Valleys and the SLO County interior Valley. Some of the 
models showed lows dipping into the upper 20s, and there is a
chance of patchy freezing temperatures, mainly in the eastern
Antelope Valley. However, more solutions showed lower to mid 30s 
and a Frost Advisory has been issued for later tonight into 
Saturday morning for the valleys mentioned above. 

Behind today's low, surface pressure gradients are trending weakly
offshore and this will help to bring a few degrees of warming to
most areas Saturday. In addition there could be some weak and
gusty northeast winds in the usual offshore wind-prone areas. By 
Saturday night the next weak system will approach the NW coast, 
spreading clouds from NW to SW over the area Saturday night. 
Starting Sunday early morning, rain chances will spread across the
area with light rain of 0.25 inch or less for some areas, with 
most areas likely to see 0.10 inch or less, through Sunday night.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...20/124 PM.

For the extended, models continue to exhibit good synoptic agreement
through the period. Main focus will be on a system moving across
the area in the Tuesday night through Wednesday night time frame.
Looking at both the deterministic and ensemble forecasts, this
system does not look too impressive at this time. For San Luis
Obispo and Santa Barbara counties, measurable rainfall looks
likely with totals of 0.10 to 0.50 inches expected (with higher
amounts around the Rocky Butte area). For Ventura and Los Angeles
counties, the chances of measurable rainfall are less and rainfall
totals, if any, would be around 0.10 inches or less. 

For Thanksgiving Day and Friday, dry conditions are expected as an
upper level ridge builds over the area and weak offshore flow
develops at the surface. High temperatures will top out in the mid
60s to mid 70s.

&&

.AVIATION...21/0616Z.

At 0455Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Good confidence in TAFs except for KPRB where there is a 40
percent chc of LIFE conds. NE to E winds are possible for KOXR, 
KCMA, KSMO, KLAX, KVNY, and KBUR. These winds may be gusty at 
times, and could create some light to moderate LLWS.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. A 7 kt east wind component is
possible through 15Z.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF. Gusty N to E are possible
through 14Z with some light LLWS.

&&

.MARINE...20/845 PM.

Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level winds are expected for the 
southern waters tonight. SCAs were extended until 3 AM for the
waters south of Point Sal. There is also the potential for a few 
lingering showers overnight tonight. Sunday, a front will move 
across the coastal waters Sunday into Monday, which could bring
isolated to scattered heavy showers. 

Another front is likely to impact the coastal waters around 
Wednesday. Best chances for wind and rain are likely to be off the
Central coast due the front weakening on approach. Post- frontal 
low-end SCA level NW-W winds will still be possible 
Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. A significant westerly
swell (around 14-16 feet) is expected mid-week, with large, SCA 
level seas for the outer waters.

&&

.BEACHES...20/845 PM.

There is significant concern for moderate to major coastal
flooding Thanksgiving week. This is due to the combination
of kelvin wave/thermal expansion, Pergiean spring tides,
and a large long-period westerly swell (260-280 degrees).

================================================================

[For Central Coast, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Tuesday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

A COASTAL FLOOD WATCH has been issued for WEDNESDAY-THURSDAY. 

The swell will arrive during this period which will combine 
with the aforementioned factors. Still some uncertainty in 
regards to how timely these will combine, but regardless 
significant impacts seem probable. Timing of peak high tides are 
expected between 845-1000AM and predicted values are:
roughly 8.2-8.6 ft for LA/VTA and 7.9-8.2 ft for Central Coast.
The reasonable worst case scenario is 0.3-0.5 ft above these
values. A slight limiting factor that may prevent the worst case
scenario from materializes would be higher mean sea level pressure.

Potential impacts if upgraded to COASTAL FLOOD WARNING:

More extensive moderate coastal flooding reaching further inland,
moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and
structures, and significant beach erosion is likely.

Areas of greatest concern: Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, 
& Cayucos/Avila/Pismo Piers. For LA: Santa Monica to Palo Verdes 
and Long Beach/Naples. For VTA, Faria to Silver Strand Beach 
including inside of harbors and Ventura Harbor. 

==================================================================

[For Santa Barbara South Coast & Catalina/Santa Barbara islands]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Thursday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

Areas of greatest concern: Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama
Beach. 

Additional Information: Elevated to high surf is likely through
Thanksgiving week. Additional coastal hazards will likely be
needed for Friday.

==================================================================

In conclusion, this is a particularly concerning period for 
coastal flooding risks - Please read the "actions" section below. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS:

(1)Heed advice from local officials - Rely on their expertise
regarding preparedness, closures, and warnings. 

(2)Protect property - Take necessary actions such as setting up
sandbags or barriers in flood-prone areas.

(3)Avoid flood areas - Stay clear of rock jetties, and flooded
roads, walkways, and other normally dry places. 

(4)Monitor the forecast for latest information: weather.gov/LOX
and @nwslosangeles on social media. Be aware of when high tide
peaks in your area: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Refer to LAXCFWLOX.
